rationale: This is a tiny, hot-loop numeric benchmark (6 functions, ~2.6 KB text) where usqrt/cubic run in tight iteration, so passes with low runtime/size overhead should dominate: SUB gets the highest weights (cheap arithmetic rewriting, strong security-per-byte, near-zero correctness risk), while SPLIT and IGV get moderate weights as low-cost diversity boosters suited to a program with few basic blocks and globals. FLA and BCF are valuable for the control-flow-heavy main/SolveCubic but their loop-hostile overhead is real in usqrt, so they carry solid SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights balanced against elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights that let the feature-driven selector apply them selectively (large/branchy functions) rather than uniformly. IBR gets moderate treatment — good indirection for a branchy cubic solver but costly in hot loops — and ICALL is kept moderate-high on DiversityGain with a raised CorrectnessRisk weight since this benchmark's few, simple calls make indirect-call wrapping safe but low-yield; all seven passes remain enabled because the program is small enough that a layered, heterogeneous defense costs little and maximizes reverse-engineering resistance without meaningfully breaching runtime or size budgets.
